headers.//: HTML must revalidate. Without this a deploy takes up to an hour to reach anyone who visited recently, which looks exactly like the change never shipped.
Fonts are immutable: the filename changes before the bytes ever do, so a year is safe and saves a revalidation on every repeat visit.

Behaviour and layout must revalidate for the same reason the HTML does. These filenames never change, so an hour of caching served fresh markup against stale scripts -- new copy with old behaviour, which looks exactly like a deploy that did not happen. no-cache still caches; it just checks first, and an unchanged file comes back as a 304.
